How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers

There are a plethora of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.

Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.
Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds

Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.

What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On , if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.
The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.
Win

The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.
Place

The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.

Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.
Show

A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.
Win/Place

Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.
Place/Show

The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.
Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)

Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.

It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.
The most popular horse racing bet types

Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).

It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.
Exactas

An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.

Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.
Trifectas

This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.
The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.
Superfectas

Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.
Super High 5

Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.
The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.
Box

A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.
For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:
- $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second
- $2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second
- $2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second
- $2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second
- $2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second
- $2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in second
You can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:
- $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third
- $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first
- $1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third
- $1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second
- $1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third
- $1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in first
From there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.
A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.
How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers

While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.
Daily Double

The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.
Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.
Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6

Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.

Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.

The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.

For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.
Understanding horse racing payouts

After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.

If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.
For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:
Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting

The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.
- October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup
- January 23, 2027: Pegasus World Cup
- March 27, 2027: Dubai World Cup
- May 1, 2027: Kentucky Derby
- May 15, 2027: Preakness Stakes
- June 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes
Triple Crown of horse racing

The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.

Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.

The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).
Tips and advice for betting on horse racing
There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.
Racing forms and past performances

Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.
Track conditions

Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.
Horse tendencies

From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.
The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.
Post position

Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.
Trainer and jockey information

A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.
Workout times
There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.
Speed figures

Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.

Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.
Manage your horse racing betting bankroll

Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.
Rules and responsible gaming

Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.

Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.
FAQ
How to bet on horse racing?

There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.
How to bet on horse racing online?
Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.
What is a box bet in horse racing?

A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.
What is a show bet in horse racing?
A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.
What is a key box bet in horse racing?

A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

articles.headline: How to solve the Cable and Battery Puzzle in We Were Here Tomorrow (Chapter 3)

body: Chapter 3 really tests your puzzle solving skills in We Were Here Tomorrow, and there’s a hard one to crack. This involves a set of cables and battery, and it can appear to be confusing at first. However, you can solve it with your partner by decoding the main trick behind it.
In this guide, I will make thing easier for you and also provide a solution for the puzzle. Thankfully, the puzzle is same for all and not random.
How to solve the Cable puzzle in We Were Here Tomorrow

There are three more module-like consoles with RED, GRE, and BLU written on them. These aren’t modules; instead, they represent locked doors unlocked by activating the correct modules.

articles.headline: France in flames is preview of what 'DSA' Democrats want for US, senator warns
keyFacts: Sen. Eric Schmitt warned that civil unrest in France is a preview of what Democrats want to happen in America.
Schmitt credited cooperation with the Trump administration for bringing new manufacturing jobs and a federal crime crackdown to Missouri.
Schmitt proposed the Modern Skies Act to fund infrastructure improvements for midsize airports like St. Louis Lambert International Airport.
body: The chaos engulfing France is a preview of what Democrats want for America, Sen. Eric Schmitt warned, contrasting the unrest with new manufacturing jobs and a federal crime crackdown in Missouri that he credits to cooperation with the Trump administration.
"You see what’s happening in France. That’s exactly what they want here, the DSA Democrats," the Missouri Republican told Fox News Digital.

His warning comes as riots, fires and looting have swept France after protests over rising living costs and strained public services turned violent, prompting curfews in parts of Paris and other cities.
"I think the Democrat Party at this point is sort of post-American and anti-Western civilization," Schmitt said.
VIOLENT FAR-LEFT RIOTS IN FRANCE ARE 'CHILLING WARNING' FOR AMERICANS AT HOME, MIKE JOHNSON SAYS
With control of the House "up for grabs," Schmitt argued, Republicans need to make the stakes clear while showing voters what they have delivered.
INSIDE THE HOUSE GOP'S 4-WEEK BATTLE PLAN TO SAVE ITS MAJORITY
Asked what a Democratic House would mean for Trump’s agenda, Schmitt accused Democrats of obstructing Republican efforts on immigration, permitting reform and regulations.
'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT FORMALLY INTRODUCES BILL TO ABOLISH ICE, BORDER PATROL AND DISMANTLE DHS

He warned that Democratic control could jeopardize funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and revive what he described as the political weaponization of government under former President Joe Biden.
But Schmitt also argued Republicans need to give voters a reason to support them, pointing to jobs and public safety as areas where he says cooperation with the Trump administration is paying off.
KEY AMERICAN INDUSTRY SEEING BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM AS TRUMP'S RE-SHORING POLICIES PAY OFF
In Missouri, he highlighted Boeing’s selection to build the Air Force’s F-47 and the Navy’s next-generation F/A-XX fighter as a potentially transformative investment in American manufacturing.
Boeing secured the Navy contract in September after winning the Air Force program last year.
BERNIE SANDERS ADMITS DEMOCRATS FAILED WORKING-CLASS VOTERS ON ECONOMICS, DRIVING THEM TO DONALD TRUMP
Schmitt, a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee , said the programs would mean 7,000 direct jobs, with additional opportunities for suppliers and surrounding businesses.
"It means that the goal we’ve been fighting for, which is that St. Louis is the defense tech capital of the United States of America, is coming true," he said.
TRUMP SAYS POLLS 'DON'T ACCOUNT FOR ONE THING,' AS HE PLEDGES TO DEFEAT COMMUNISTS 'ONCE AND FOR ALL'
Schmitt said he worked with Trump and administration officials to help land the programs, describing them as "generational opportunities" for Missouri workers.
"You think of the good-paying jobs that’s going to mean for generations to come, it’s just a game changer," he said.
He also tied the aircraft programs to the broader competition with China, saying the next generation of fighters would help meet military demands in the Pacific.

On public safety, Schmitt pointed to Operation Show Me Justice , an ATF-led enforcement surge that resulted in 435 arrests and the seizure of 166 firearms in St. Louis, according to the Justice Department.
Authorities also seized 81 kilograms of drugs and more than $1.25 million linked to suspected illegal gun and drug transactions during the operation, which officials announced had concluded Oct. 15.
Schmitt said his conversations with administration officials have carried a straightforward request for his hometown.
TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY
"St. Louis, we need your help," he said.
The former Missouri attorney general described the toll of violence on families, including grandparents cleaning up broken glass and parents burying their children.
"We don’t need to accept this," he said. "We just don’t need to accept the idea that violent crime needs to be in the headlines every single day."
He pledged the effort would continue beyond the surge.
"This isn’t a one-and-done deal. There are more resources coming," Schmitt said.
OMAR'S NEW LEGISLATION TARGETING ICE SPARKS OUTRAGE WHEN THE INTERNET SEES WHAT'S IN IT: 'UN-AMERICAN'
For families wanting to send children safely to school, visit a park or attend a Cardinals game downtown, he said the goal is a better quality of life.
"I think the message is help is on the way, and there are real tangible results now, not just rhetoric, not just empty promises," Schmitt said.
"We’re not letting up."
Schmitt’s third major priority is modernizing St. Louis Lambert International Airport, an effort he linked to the region’s aerospace growth and aviation history.

His Modern Skies Act would fund improvements to air traffic control technology, towers and airport terminals. He said midsize airports need help securing investments that larger hubs can more readily finance.
"St. Louis is the gateway to the West," he said. "It deserves a world-class airport."
The proposal remains a legislative push rather than a guaranteed funding award for Lambert. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during an October visit that airport funding would be competitive.
For Schmitt, those priorities form part of the argument Republicans need to make as voters weigh control of Congress.
He cast the election as "common sense versus crazy," but cautioned that Republicans cannot assume their supporters will show up.
"I just don’t think you can take anything for granted," Schmitt said. "I think we have to fight for every vote and tell an important story."
"I think if we do that, we’re gonna hold on to the Senate, and the House is up for grabs."

articles.headline: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
keyFacts: Microsoft launched a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases for Xbox Insiders, allowing non-subscribers to stream eligible games they already own.
Introductory prices range from 24 to 40 cents per hour depending on the size of the purchased playtime pack.
Microsoft stated that purchased playtime remains available until it is used and does not expire.
body: In September, when Microsoft severely limited the game-streaming buffet available to Game Pass subscribers, the company said non-subscribers would soon be able to “purchase cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and stream eligible games they own on supported devices.” Today, Microsoft rolled out those a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases to Xbox Insiders, with prices that might be a bit galling for players who have already purchased these streamable games.
The “introductory launch pricing” for Xbox’s Cloud Playtime purchases is as follows:
- 10 hours for $4 (~$0.40/hour)
- 25 hours for $8 (~$0.32/hour)
- 50 hours for $12 (~$0.24/hour)
Purchased playtime “remains available until it’s used,” Microsoft writes, so you don’t have to worry about your 50-hour purchase expiring before you can use it fully.

Paying for playtime directly like this evokes images of old arcades, where players would invest a quarter or two (in 20th century dollars) often for just a few minutes of gameplay. That kind of metered play has fallen heavily out of fashion, though, in favor of one-time purchases for an all-you-can-play experience at home.

On the surface, paying as low as 24 cents for an hour of streaming game time doesn’t sound completely unreasonable. Remember, though, that these streaming costs come on top of whatever you paid to buy the game in the first place. Unlike an Xbox Game Pass subscription—which includes a few hours of monthly streaming access to hundreds of games as part of the subscription price—these Cloud Playtime packs “require cloud playable game purchase or, for select games, free-to-play access,” Microsoft writes.
Say what you will about the old arcade model, but you didn’t have to buy the cabinet and then pay a quarter per play.
Keep the meter running

Microsoft’s metered Cloud Playtime packs differ from Google’s failed Stadia streaming experiment, which offered unlimited streaming playtime across devices for games you purchased on the platform. Of course, Stadia game purchases also didn’t let you download games for local play on a PC or console, making the overall value proposition quite different. That was especially true after Stadia’s 2022 shutdown made those purchases unplayable (though Google offered full refunds for any and all Stadia purchases at that point).

articles.headline: The 3-in-1 Alloop Wearable Could Replace Both Your Wellness Wristband and Ring
keyFacts: Alloop announced a modular health wearable system on Wednesday that can be worn as a wristband or a ring.
The device features a personal AI health agent powered by Google Gemini and ChatGPT and operates without a mandatory subscription.
The Alloop Trio will launch on November 10 as a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign priced at $299.
body: This wearables industry has become increasingly saturated with smart rings and wrist-based fitness trackers, so any company that wants to compete in the space has to get creative. Enter Alloop, a modular, AI-native health wearable announced on Wednesday.
According to a press release, Alloop can be worn in three ways. The company calls this the Trio.

As part of the Trio, there are four pieces of hardware. There’s a wristband, a ring, the Cube — a compact sensor system that collects your health data — and Halo, which offers tap-to-speak, light, color patterns and haptic feedback to communicate reminders, device information, your wellness status and more.
More from CNET

You can wear the wristband with both the Cube and Halo for extra feedback and to log with your voice; the wristband with just the Cube for a lighter, more discreet wrist-based design; or snap the Cube into the ring for the most compact version of the wearable, ideal for sleep.
What Alloop measures

The Cube’s sensors measure resting heart rate, heart rate variability, blood oxygen, breathing rate and temperature. You can also log your meals and supplements using photos, voice or text. Collectively, this allows Alloop to provide a sleep score and information about nutrition, activity, strain, recovery and health trends.
Compatible with iOS and Android, the Alloop app’s health dashboard brings key data into a unified view.

There’s also Bio Age, which uses 18 measurements across six health categories, including nutrition, bodily signals and lifestyle, to determine your biological age and show the factors contributing to it. As opposed to one’s chronological age, biological age estimates how you’re supposedly aging at the cellular level.
Alloop AI

The Alloop Trio was built around a personal AI health agent. You can log your meals, symptoms, feelings and more using text, voice and images, while Alloop AI connects that information to the health data collected by the Cube’s sensors and then uses it to offer guidance, proactive insights, personalized plans and more.
This is similar to how AI agents created by other wearable companies work.
It uses Google Gemini and ChatGPT, an Alloop spokesperson said.
Subscription-free

Alloop described the Trio in its press release as an open health platform, as, unlike other fitness trackers, its app doesn’t require a subscription. However, there will also be an optional Pro plan with usage-based access levels, costing about $5 per month.

While the free plan will serve the vast majority of people for everyday health management and light conversational AI use, the Pro plan will provide more in-depth health-related research and enhanced personal agent capabilities.
“By drawing on a user’s longer-term data, health goals, daily behaviors and interaction context, Pro will support deeper insights and more personalized planning,” the Alloop spokesperson said.

Supported integrations include the ability to import data from medical records, lab tests, continuous glucose monitors and third-party wearables and health apps, including Apple Health and Google Health.
Privacy

According to the press release, Alloop “specifies health data protection across collection, transfer, storage and management, with controls that let users review, delete and export their data.” The company’s privacy policy adds that it doesn’t sell personal information and that health and wellness information isn’t used for advertising or marketing.
“Our policy is to keep US users’ data within the United States, without transferring it overseas,” said the Alloop spokesperson.

The company is developing its privacy and security practices to meet the requirements of the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation and the California Consumer Privacy Act, with the goal of completing a SOC 2 examination and obtaining ISO/IEC 27001 certification. SOC 2 is a voluntary compliance standard for safeguarding customer data, while ISO/IEC 27001 is a global standard for information security management systems.
However, you should always exercise caution and read the fine print before sharing your health data with any company or AI agent.
Community

There will be a community feature that allows you to share your progress and see others’ across workouts, meals, daily life and health routines and protocols. You can also create groups, take part in shared challenges and chat with each other in the Alloop app.

Alloop’s privacy policy states that when you use the community features, the company collects profile information, follows, posts, images, comments, reactions, feed activity and messages, which can help it respond to reports, enforce community rules and protect you from spam, abuse and security threats. Depending on the feature and visibility settings, the information you publish may be visible to others.
Price and availability
The Alloop Trio will launch on Nov. 10 as a crowdfunding campaign on Kickstarter. Subject to change, the crowdfunding price is $299.
Shipping is estimated for late December 2026 to early January 2027.

articles.headline: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
keyFacts: Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice scored in the 82nd minute to secure a draw against Bayern Munich.
Harry Kane provided an assist and scored a penalty to put Bayern Munich ahead during the match.
Eberechi Eze initially gave Arsenal the lead in the first half before Bayern mounted their comeback.
body: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own.

Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged.

Enter Kane. He wore his playmaker’s hat; some of his passing was sumptuous and it was his assist for Alphonso Davies that helped Bayern to draw level. He wore his finisher’s one, too, scoring from the penalty spot to put his team in charge. It meant he had scored in 10 consecutive Champions League games; one short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. There is a reason why Kane is the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday. He now has 16 goals against Arsenal; he has only scored more against one club – Leicester, against whom he has 20.

Rice loosened Bayern’s grip. It was a lovely goal from him and Arsenal even hinted at a late winner, Jurriën Timber drawing a tip over from Manuel Neuer in stoppage time. That would have been too much because Bayern shaded an absorbing tie in terms of clear chances created. But Arsenal made their point. They were value for it.

Arsenal knew they were inside a fortress. Bayern had not previously lost a Champions League group or league phase match at their own stadium since the 3-2 reverse against Manchester City in December 2013, 40 games ago. The following 39 featured 37 wins and two draws. Arteta’s players were not intimidated. They bristled with assurance at the outset and Rice rewarded their never-say-die spirit. Bayern had wanted revenge for their 3-1 defeat at the Emirates Stadium in the league stage last season. They did not get it.

Arteta’s idea was to go pretty much as strong as possible with his lineup. He made just two changes, Timber for Ben White and Noni Madueke for Eze, albeit the latter was not on the bench for long. Saka had tussled with Davies and it looked innocuous. The alarm bells rang when Saka grabbed his thigh and went to ground, waving his hand in the air.

Was it possible for the Arsenal support to think that Bayern had been stripped of their fear factor in the line behind Kane? Michael Olise was suspended, Jamal Musiala was injured and Luis Díaz was a substitute. He came on in the 68th minute only to be forced off before the end. Bayern were without the midfielder Joshua Kimmich for personal reasons.

Arteta moved Madueke over to his more natural position on the right wing when he introduced Eze on the left and Bayern will still be wondering how the latter was afforded so much space up the inside channel on that flank to put Arsenal in front.

It was a fabulous ball from Martin Ødegaard, who was in the mood, full of sharp turns and urgency, and Eze had the time to let it bounce before shooting first time into the far corner. An offside flag killed the Arsenal celebrations and there was one of those weird waits before the video assistant referee ruled that Eze was in fact onside.

Kane was booed by the Arsenal fans. Of course he was. He dropped deep to link the play and there was a moment in the 17th minute when he started a move with a pass from inside his own penalty area. There was a glorious ping over Gabriel Magalhães, who was the last Arsenal defender, for Ismael Saibari on 23 minutes, although his teammate could not control, and Kane’s fingerprints were all over the equaliser. He was on halfway when he sculpted the low through ball for Davies which took Timber out of the equation. The Bayern winger’s finish was clinical.

Bayern had other chances in the first half, none better than the one for Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, in the 21st minute. It was Kane who began the attack, taking a quick goal kick – yes, really – and Gnabry was the man over on the right when the Bayern forwards worked it that way. Gnabry’s shot was too close to David Raya. Kane also saw Ezri Konsa produce a fine block to keep him out.

It is never anything other than a pleasure to be at the Allianz for a showpiece match. All the staples were present and correct. The en masse scarf waving. The slightly slapstick oompah band notes. The fans at either end of the ground calling to each other. The non-stop drumbeat and songs from the Südkurve, who also bounced as one at times.

The pre-game surprise had been the sight of Vincent Kompany in the Bayern dugout; the manager made a Lazarus-like rise from his sickbed and the action after the restart kept the blood pumping. Arsenal thought they had gone back ahead when Bruno Guimarães rose to meet Rice’s corner only for Neuer to produce an extraordinary save.

The goalkeeper touched the ball up and on to the crossbar and away. Shades of Gordon Banks against Pelé. It was Raya’s turn next; his save to keep out Dayot Upamecano’s close-range header from Gnabry’s cross was of the highest order.

It was interesting to watch Kane after the penalty was awarded for handball against Timber. Bayern had worked the ball back to their No 9 and, when he shot, Timber’s arm was outstretched. Kane went through his mental processes. He could see that Raya did not retreat to his line for what felt like an age. Kane delayed even longer. He was in total control. He stuttered before banging the ball hard into the right-hand corner.

Bayern were close to putting the game to bed. Konrad Laimer dragged narrowly past the far post when well-placed but it was Arsenal who produced the sucker punch. Eze was dangerous throughout. And when the opportunity knocked for Rice after a pass from the substitute Viktor Gyökeres, he made no mistake.

articles.headline: Your Favorite Video Games Will Always Be Influenced By Manga
keyFacts: The Brooklyn Museum in New York City is hosting the Art of Manga exhibit, curated by Nicole Coolidge Rousmaniere, from October 3, 2026, to January 31, 2027.
The exhibition features works from 10 prominent manga artists, including Jiro Taniguchi, Rumiko Takahashi, Eiichiro Oda, and Hirohiko Araki.
The article highlights how manga heavily influences video games, noting specific connections to titles like Persona, Dark Souls, and Yakuza: Like a Dragon.
body: In the heart of Brooklyn, there is now a devastatingly gorgeous manga panel from Jiro Taniguchi's Ice Age: Chronicle of the Earth hung on a gallery wall. I can't tell you what it says--I fear my scant familiarity with Japanese doesn't extend to literacy in kanji--but I can tell you what it portrays: a cityscape consumed by nature. A lush tangle of vines and trees reclaiming the Earth from its disastrous, mettlesome inheritors.

While I doubt this panel and manga are the first time this kind of image has cropped up, it certainly feels like a progenitor to many similar visuals across the years. Your mind might jump to I Am Legend, the Will Smith-led feature film about a post-apocalyptic New York City, for example. My mind jumped straight to Nier Automata's city that's been lost to time, as well as The Last of Us' many dilapidated small towns and US metropolises. Though I went into the Brooklyn Museum's new Art of Manga exhibit already curious about what connections the form might have to games, it became quickly apparent that manga has always been in conversation with other mediums, influencing everything from anime to gaming.

The Brooklyn Museum, located right near Prospect Park in New York City, is currently home to the Art of Manga exhibit. Curated by Nicole Coolidge Rousmaniere--whose love of manga stems from early exposure to French graphic novels and reading Astro Boy at a seminal age--the gallery features a beautiful selection of Taniguchi’s work, as well as select other notable mangaka (manga artists and authors) of outsized influence. This includes Rumiko Takahashi, best known for her work on Ranma ½ and Inuyasha, Eiichiro Oda, the renowned creator of One Piece, and Hirohiko Araki, whose gorgeously styled illustrations from Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure are among the exhibits crown jewels.

In total, the exhibit draws from the work of 10 mangaka , evenly split between male and female authors of varying popularity and prefectures of Japan, and explores different kinds of subject matter including inner-city living and queer life. This was essential to Rousmaniere, As she explained, "If I had featured fewer artists, the exhibition would not have been as powerful; We might not have gotten across the incredible range of these artists and the power of the line that they employ." The Art of Manga exhibit, evidently, needed to be big.

And big it is. At its center, there is a reading room with bookshelves full of manga related to the artists spotlighted in the exhibit. Whole walls are adorned with iconic illustrations of some of the manga (a particularly poignant scene from One Piece comes to mind near the exhibit's end), but some of the highlighted art is also quite grand. Jojo's Bizarre Adventure, for example, is the subject of what Rousmaniere calls "the heart of the exhibition:" a 12-panel composition called "There is always a Traitor." The work consists of a series of life-sized panels of Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure’s Stand users assembled in tableau, with each panel towering over the average visitor and making the cast out to be even larger than life than they typically are. Or as Rousmaniere puts it, Araki's "2D figures are in fact 3D, and jump from the page into our imagination."

"What I adore about Araki Hirohiko is his versatility and his ability to embrace new challenges, be it life-size painting or lithography, fashion, or music. He has no bounds on his imagination and I think this is what makes him and his work so vital," Rousmaniere extolled.

A little ways away from that massive installation is a smaller piece from Araki that might look strikingly similar to many gamers. In it, many characters from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure stand huddled up on what appears to be a bus. The distinct juxtaposition of the cast's bright colors and exotic patterns against the drab gray of the bus interior cuts an imposing image. To the eye of your average RPG player, like me, the ensemble might look eerily close to that of a Persona game.

If you’re anything like me, you probably can’t look at Araki’s work without immediately drawing connections to Persona , a beloved RPG series from Atlus that touts, among many other things, an impeccable sense of forward-thinking fashion and style on par with the closets of characters like Jotaro and Jolyne.

But that’s not all they have in common. The two also share a penchant for the supernatural and mythological, and both casts can summon powerful beings in battle. In the manga of JJBA, these forces are known as Stands, but in the world of Persona, they are called … well, Persona. The creators of the Persona games have never outright confirmed the influence of JJBA on the production of the series, but their lineage feels like an unspoken truth.

Manga's influence on games doesn't begin or end there, either. The mangaka of Dragon Ball, the late Akira Toriyama, literally helped sculpt the visual identity of both the Dragon Quest series and Chrono Trigger, two early successes for the companies that were then known separately as Square and Enix. Beyond that, it feels like the sensibilities and attitudes of these games and that era of RPG--the fascination with small-town living and domesticity for example--owe something to the genial nature of Toriyama's characters and the warm fantasy tapestry he helped to create.

Alternatively, much later RPGs feel like direct descendants of Berserk, the late Kentaro Miura’s manga, which has been a huge influence in the rise of dark fantasy. Miura's bleak fantasy epic has long served as a muse of sorts for a whole class of character in the Final Fantasy series, and has also been a major touchstone for From Software’s oeuvre like Dark Souls and Elden Ring.

Of course, manga has also paved the way for anime, which often reimagines and reinterprets manga and has made global phenomena of many works, such as One Piece. One Piece has become one of the best-known brands since its anime adaptation enraptured the world, and now there are One Piece nights at baseball games! I can’t walk to one of my local trains without seeing a plush of Chopper in a neighbor’s window or a straw-hat ornament on a passerby's bag. And when you see Oda’s art on display in Brooklyn Museum’s exhibit, including an illustration that explicitly features Nami and Usopp playing video games featuring some very familiar caricatures, it’s easy to see why the series and its cast have inspired such awe across the world and artistic mediums.

The camaraderie between Luffy and his friends, which serves as the emotional core of the series, is aspirational and has seemingly served as the template for one of gaming’s more recent band of oddities. In an interview with Crunchyroll , the newest head of Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio (and longtime writer) Masayoshi Yokoyama admitted that the cast of Yakuza: Like a Dragon, the game that transformed the brawler series into a turn-based RPG, was molded after Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates.

Yokoyama told Crunchyroll at the time, "To me, Ichiban is basically Luffy. And around him there’s Zoro and Nami and basically the rest of the party, you know? One Piece’s party composition was on my mind so much during writing that it was a massive influence." It feels like Yokoyama's only scratching the surface with that comparison too. As two long-running series that often painstakingly shift perspectives to illuminate struggles against unfair systems and institutions, I don’t think it’s the only way that the two are alike.

Even if it is indirect, or I guess roundabout in this case, manga's force has become increasingly undeniable over the years. Rousmaniere shared, "When I was in Japan in the '80s, everyone was reading manga. I was studying archaeology and the archaeologists mostly all read manga. Manga captures the zeitgeist of a moment that other forms do not in a tangible, and not fleeting, fashion." As it's bled into anime with increasing success, manga's influence has only grown. Now it is, per Rousmaniere, "in Barnes and Noble in the US, in Waterstones in the UK, and in airports around the country." It's everywhere.

Though the Art of Manga exhibit may not overtly draw attention to the forms’ ties to games, there is one outstanding reference to the modern gaming landscape that’s hard to ignore. Before you enter the exhibit, right outside the entrance to Brooklyn Museum’s gift shop that is now itself adorned with manga-inspired merch and paraphernalia, there is an army of gashapon ("gacha") machines that visitors are encouraged to play. I clocked everything from Digimon to My Hero Academia and more among the capsule-sized toys and charms that players could pull.

"Many people watch gamers just as I enjoy watching visitors and museum workers choosing their gashapon at the front of the store," Rousmaniere shared, drawing an interesting line from her enjoyment of seeing people turn their fascination with manga into a literal keepsake to how one might enjoy watching a streamer try pulling a legendary roll in a gacha game like Genshin Impact. That gashapon machines, whose mechanics have become the basis for countless popular video games in the last decade, just so happen to be halfway between manga and gaming makes their prominent inclusion here quite serendipitous.

My big takeaway from the Art of Manga exhibit? Art goes beyond frames and borders, touches other artists and mediums outside of itself all the time, and continues spreading regardless of genres, nations, or any other manner of restraint. In some ways, you can draw an incredibly clear line from manga to games, like Araki's work and something like Persona. In other ways, the influence might be felt but not obviously seen. But it's always worth exploring other forms and, for instance, walking through a gallery like this one and interrogating where it all might stem from.
Brooklyn Museum's Art of Manga exhibit runs from October 3, 2026 to January 31, 2027.

articles.headline: Democrats have 11-point lead among likely voters as Trump’s approval rating craters – live
keyFacts: Likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans by 11 percentage points, according to New York Times and Siena University polling.
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty after a jury found it deceived users about data privacy.
Donald Trump will continue his campaign blitz in South Carolina for Republican Senate nominee Darline Graham before the midterm elections.
body: Democrats have 11-point lead among likely voters as Trump’s approval rating craters – live
New poll finds likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans running for office by 11 percentage points; Trump campaigns in South Carolina
New polling shows likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans, fewer than two weeks until midterm elections
New polling from the New York Times and Siena University shows that likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans running for office by 11 percentage points.
Meanwhile, Donald Trump’s approval rating dropped to a new low for this particular survey – 36%.

Notably, according to the Times’ polling, the perception of either party has shifted over the last two years. The number of people who consider Democrats as the party of the working class has grown by five points – from 48% to 53%, while it’s dropped by five points for Republicans – from 45% to 40%.
Musk threatens to 'come for' Democrats who 'pick fights' with him in new Congress
Elon Musk – the tech billionaire, Trump ally, and founder of Tesla and Space X – has threatened to home in on Democrats who pursue him in the next Congress.

“Live by the sword, die by the sword,” Musk wrote on X, the social media platform he bought in 2022. “Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets.”

This comes after Politico reported earlier today that Democratic lawmakers were considering how best to investigate Musk, and his businesses, if the party gains control of Congress following the midterm elections.

US envoy Steve Witkoff announced this morning that Russia authorities had freed Stephen Hubbard, the first American known to be convicted of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine. Hubbard was arrested when the Russians briefly took over the Ukrainian city of Izium at the start of the ongoing conflict in 2022.

Donald Trump welcomed the news,noting the prisoner release was the result of a direct request he made to Putin in a telephone call last week. Meanwhile, after Witkoff’s discussions with Putin in St Petersburg, he flattered the Russian president by calling him a “humanitarian”. The emissary’s comments drew bipartisan backlash, but Trump defended them: “I guess you could say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life, out,” the US president told reporters in the East Room.

Witkoff also said that his discussions with Putin were “constructive”, and“will continue with trilateral talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine at the technical level”. This comes after Trump’s reignited feud with Zelenskyy after he urged Kyiv to end its attacks on Russian refineries and waived sweeping sanctions against Moscow.

New polling from the New York Times and Siena University shows thatlikely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans running for office by 11 percentage points. Meanwhile, Trump’s approval rating dropped to a new low for this particular survey – 36%.

At a campaign rally in Cincinnati, Ohio, JD Vance criticized the media and Democrats for focusing on Vivek Ramaswamy’s recent ad for his gubernatorial campaign, which features the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent,Amy Acton. The vice-president defended Ramaswamy for having “the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is, and calls Amy Acton a liar”. Donna Arthur, Acton’s mother, claimed in the spot that her daughter “lied her entire life” about living in a tent during her childhood. However, Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, said on Tuesday that his sister is estranged from her mother, who had married a man that sexually abused Acton when she was 12 years old. Arthur, he said, remained in the marriage even after her husband was arrested and her children were taken away from her.

The supreme court has refused to allow the Trump administration to immediately deny gender-affirming care for transgender people in federal prisons. The decision leaves in place a lower-court block on the policy while a legal challenge plays out. It was adopted after an executive order from Trump, who’s taken several steps to roll back transgender rights during his second term.

With 13 days until the midterms,Trump will continue his campaign blitz by heading to Clemson, South Carolina, where he’ll rally for Darline Graham – the Republican nominee for US Senate who is hoping to secure a full term for her late brother’s seat. Darline was appointed by the South Carolina governor to carry out the remainder of Lindsey Graham’s time in office after his death in July. However, she now faces a competitive race against Annie Andrews, a pediatrician and the Democratic nominee, in a contest that has become increasingly rancorous in recent months.
Trump defends special envoy Witkoff calling Putin a 'humanitarian'
In the East Room today, Trump defended Steve Witkoff’s comments, noting that the release of Steven Hubbard might warrant praise for Putin.
“I guess you could say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life, out,” Trump told reporters.

Earlier, we noted that Thom Tillis, the outgoing Republican senator from North Carolina, slammed special envoy Steve Witkoff for calling Vladimir Putin a “humanitarian” today – following the release of detained US citizen Steven Hubbard.
Now, more GOP lawmakers are pushing back.
“Vladimir Putin is not our friend, and he is certainly no humanitarian,” said retiring Republican senator Joni Ernst.
She added: “His relentless attacks on innocent civilians in Ukraine show his total disregard for human life. Appeasement won’t end this war. Pressure will.”

With 13 days until the midterms, early voting data is rolling in nationwide. Democrats need to net four Senate seats and hold 218 House seats to reclaim a congressional majority. Here is where the numbers stand so far:

Turnout is surging in key battlegrounds: Over 16 million Americans have already voted in person or by mail. According to the University of Florida’s Election Lab, battleground states -including Michigan, Ohio, Georgia, Texas, Florida and North Carolina – have each passed 700,000 ballots cast as of 21 October. Turnout is being driven in part by widespread voter frustration, reflected in Donald Trump’s record-low approval ratings.

Democrats lead in early returns: Registered Democrats account for 47% of early ballots cast, compared with 29% from Republicans (tracking returned ballots, not candidate selection). The party gap is most pronounced in North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. While Republicans traditionally favor election day voting, strategists worry this widened margin signals a “red undertow” – GOP voters staying home due to frustration over high gas prices, the conflict in Iran and sweeping tariffs.

Early votes are pacing well ahead of 2022: In Georgia, early votes already represent nearly 30% of the total turnout from the 2022 midterms. Florida sits at 18%, with similarly high paces recorded in North Carolina, Michigan and Ohio.

Mail-in voting remains resilient: Over 56m mail-in ballots have been requested or sent nationally – greater than the 52m requested in 2022, according to NBC News (using data from TargetSmart). Despite executive orders from the Trump administration attempting to restrict mail-in voting, which the supreme court struck down in September, voters continue to utilize the process at pre-pandemic rates.
Meta ordered to pay $25bn penalty over deceiving users about data privacy

A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn in penalties, on after a jury found the company had misled consumers in a case arising from allegations that Cambridge Analytica – a political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign – obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.

The state’s attorney general had sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm, had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

“Facebook’s wrongdoing – over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public – goes to the heart of Facebook’s core business practices,” Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order following the verdict.
Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219bn was warranted, based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25bn.

In Maine, Susan Collins, the moderate Republican incumbent senator vying for a sixth term in office, joined the growing list of GOP lawmakers to urge the Trump administration to reverse the waiving of Russian sanctions.

“First of all the law is very clear, that we wanted additional sanctions to be imposed on Russia, by cutting the deal on diesel with Russia. [Trump] is not going to increase the supply to the United States in any measurable way. But what he is going to do is to get more funding for Russia to use to attack Ukraine,” Collins told reporters in Lewiston, where she was joined by former independent senator Joe Manchin for a campaign stop.
Vance criticizes outrage over Ramaswamy ad featuring opponent's estranged mother

At a campaign rally in Cincinnati, Ohio, JD Vance criticized the media and Democrats for focusing on Vivek Ramaswamy’s recent ad for his gubernatorial campaign, which features the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton.

As we noted earlier, the campaign spot, which has circulated among conservatives on social media, shows Donna Arthur, Acton’s mother, claiming that her daughter “lied her entire life” about spending time living in a tent during her childhood.

However, Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, blasted the ad, and said his sister is estranged from her mother, who had married a man that sexually abused Acton when she was 12 years old. Arthur, he said, remained in the marriage even after her husband was arrested and her children were taken away from her.
Today, Vance defended Ramaswamy for having “the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it isand calls Amy Acton a liar”.
Vance added: “My message, ladies and gentlemen, is very simple. Whatever you think about any of the TV advertisements, focus on the substance and focus on the facts.”
Witkoff calls meeting with Putin 'constructive', says trilateral talks will continue 'at the technical level'

Special envoy Steve Witkoff said his meeting today with Vladimir Putin – which resulted in the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old former teacher who had spent more than four years in Russian jails– was “constructive”.

Trump’s emissary met with Russian leadership in St Petersburg, after talks in Oslo with Zelenskyy and Nordic leaders. The Ukrainian president has pushed for an in-person meeting with Moscow and Washington to hammer out a lasting peace deal, as fighting rages on.
Witkoff added that his discussions today “will continue with trilateral talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine at the technical level”.

“While there is still important work left to do, President Trump remains committed to seeing this war end and achieving a comprehensive, durable peace that will provide security and prosperity for generations to come,” Witkoff said, following the president’s reignited feud with Zelenskyy after he urged Kyiv to end its attacks on Russian refineries and waived sweeping sanctions against Moscow.
A 24-year-old Kansas man has been arrested for allegedly threatening to shoot Donald Trump.

Authorities arrested Jaden J Read, of Clearwater, Kansas, last Saturday after he allegedly posted threats to kill the US president at his rally in the Wichita area on Monday, according to the justice department.

According to federal authorities, a Crime Stoppers tip on 15 October led investigators to a Facebook post responding to a KAKE News article about Trump’s upcoming Wichita visit. Read allegedly commented: “Let’s shoot Trump honestly, where’s our shooter? I’m tired of living this money life.”
Immediately afterward, he allegedly posted a second comment on the same article: “I just got a 308 and 305 round and I’m killing this pedo.”
Authorities also found two additional comments allegedly posted by Read in response to a KWCH 12 News article about Trump’s planned visit.

“Can we shoot him in Kansas please I will myself,” Read allegedly wrote. A minute later, he allegedly posted another comment, saying: “IK where your speech will be. Already mapped out roofs around. Finna get kirked since yall couldn’t help him.”

Read was arrested in Clearwater last Saturday and taken into federal custody, where he will remain pending a detention hearing. The district of Kansas filed a criminal complaint against Read for making threats against the president.
Retiring GOP senator Thom Tillis has ridiculed DonaldTrump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff for praising Vladimir Putinas a “humanitarian”.
“WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of ‘humanitarian,’” Tillis said in a post on X, with a screenshot showing the definition.

“What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say,” the North Carolina senator went on. “You should go back to Ukraine and ask the families of the children Putin has kidnapped and murdered whether they agree your friend Putin is a ‘humanitarian.’”

Elena Kagan criticized rulings made by the US supreme court’s conservative majority this week, arguing that its recent decisions on redistricting and campaign finance had undermined America’s democracy.

“The court has kind of blinded itself to the very deleterious effects of their rulings on how the political system works,” said Kagan, one of the court’s three liberal justices, during a discussion at Catholic University’s law school in Washington DC yesterday, according to multiple reports.
She emphasized that the court, which has a 6-3 conservative majority, “has created a democracy that does not work as well as it should”.

Kagan’s remarks come just two weeks before the midterm elections and amid battles over congressional redistricting. Earlier this year, the supreme court struck down Louisiana’s congressional map, effectively gutting a major section of the Voting Rights Act. In June, the court also struck down campaign finance restrictions limiting how much political parties may spend on candidates. Both decisions were split 6-3 along ideological lines.

As a result, she said, “both political parties have been engaged in a race to the bottom in terms of doing these partisan gerrymanders, effectively depriving masses of citizens of their rights to voting equality”.
Kagan said that decision was pushing political candidates “away from the center, toward the wings, toward the extremes, because the only thing anybody has to worry about any more is being primaried”.

“It is making what I think is unfortunately a too polarized country even more so,” she continued. “In this election, and the next election, we are seeing large states with substantial numbers of people who vote for Republicans and who vote for Democrats, and the states are going to be tried to turn all red or all blue in a way that I think is very destructive to our democracy.”
Kagan also criticized the court’s decisions on campaign finance rules, and the increasing amounts of money in politics.
The people of America look around this political system and think that all this money chasing all these political candidates is a nightmare. And they’re right.
Supreme court rebuffs Trump restrictions on medical care for trans inmates for now
The supreme court has refused to allow the Trump administration to immediately deny gender-affirming care for transgender people in federal prisons.

The decision leaves in place a lower-court block on the policy while a legal challenge plays out. It was adopted after an executive order from Donald Trump, who’s taken several steps to roll back transgender rights during his second term.
Two of the supreme court’s six conservative justices, Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, dissented, meaning they would have allowed the policy to be enforced.

Trump’s January 2025 executive order called on the Bureau of Prisons to revise its medical care policies so federal funds aren’t spent “for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of the opposite sex”.
The new policy would halt surgical and hormonal treatments, and end “social accommodations” like makeup and wigs. Prisons would continue to offer mental health services.
Trans prisoners sued the administration over the policy and, so far, two lower courts have blocked officials from implementing the order as the larger lawsuit over the executive order continues.
Steve Witkoff lavished praise on Vladimir Putin during their meeting at the grand Constantine Palace in St Petersburg, describing the Russian president as a humanitarian.

“You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Trump’s special envoy told Putin. He also conveyed Trump’s thanks for a deal to resume Russian diesel exports to the US.

The Russian president is wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) as a war criminal, in relation to the deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia during the war. More than 17,500 civilians have been confirmed killed in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to the UN, which says the true toll is likely to be significantly higher.

The warmth of Witkoff’s remarks stood in stark contrast to the increasingly hostile rhetoric directed at Volodymyr Zelenskyy by senior US officials, most notably Trump, who has called for the Ukrainian president to resign and portrayed him as the main obstacle to peace.

Witkoff travelled to Russia from Oslo, where he had met Zelenskyy and European leaders a day earlier in an attempt to inject momentum into stalled negotiations, with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine now in its fifth year.
Witkoff told Putin during a televised portion of their meeting:
We’ve brought some papers. It’s really some ideas, some sort of peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, and you’ll read that at your leisure.
The visit was Witkoff’s ninth to Russia since Trump tasked him with brokering an end to the war.
A White House official has confirmed to the Guardian that Donald Trump’s roundtable at 2.30pm ET will be focused on cybercrime.

The president is “unleashing every available tool to stop foreign-based organized criminal organizations that exploit Americans in cyberspace”, the official said in a statement. “The most vulnerable among us – seniors, children, and low-income families – are disproportionately targeted, with scammers draining life savings, stealing the benefits of years of work, and destroying lives.”
According to the FBI, Americans reported losing almost $21bn to cybercrime and internet scams.
While Donald Trump will be in South Carolina today, his vice-president, JD Vance, will be stumping in Cincinnati, Ohio.

The Buckeye state is home to a must-keep Senate seat for Republicans, where the incumbent, John Husted, is fending off a challenge from former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown – the populist hoping for a comeback.

The state’s gubernatorial competition has also become increasingly bitter. On Tuesday, my colleague Chris Stein reported that the family of Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio, is criticizing her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy for using Acton’s estranged mother in a recently released campaign ad.
In the ad, which has circulated among conservatives on social media, Actons’s mother, Donna Arthur, said: “She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true. She’s lied her entire life.”

In a Tuesday statement, Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, said his sister is estranged from her mother, who had married a man that sexually abused Acton when she was 12 years old. He added that Arthur remained in the marriage even after her husband was arrested and her children were taken away from her.

“It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” he said in a statement released by Acton’s campaign.
Trump praises UK approval of controversial Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
Donald Trump has welcomed the news that UK government has approved the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea.

“Great news for the wealth and prosperity of the United Kingdom, and the wonderful region of Aberdeen. The UK has started drilling in the North Sea, one of the greatest and most prosperous areas of OIL in the World,” the US president wrote on Truth Social.
He added that the UK should go “FULL BLAST”, and the move to resume offshore extraction would “make the UK very wealthy again”.

As my colleagues reported earlier today, Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister, said the Jackdaw project will “protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm this winter”. This comes after fierce opposition from several Labour MPs and environmental groups throughout the country.

Trump has long pushed for Britain to expand oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, instead of relying on wind turbines. He frequently clashed with Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer, who argued that energy sustainability relied on renewable sources and moving away from fossil fuel dependence.

articles.headline: Gavin Newsom gets brutal exit report card as 62% of California voters are begging for a new direction: poll
keyFacts: A new poll found that 62 percent of California registered voters rate Governor Gavin Newsom's overall performance as fair or poor.
Voters gave Newsom negative ratings on homelessness, housing, and taxes, while his spokesperson highlighted his past election victories.
In the upcoming gubernatorial race, Democrat Xavier Becerra leads Republican Steve Hilton 55 percent to 35 percent among likely voters, the poll found.
body: Gavin Newsom is leaving Sacramento with a damning report card.

A new poll finds 62% of California registered voters rate his tenure fair or poor, with voters panning his handling of homelessness, housing, taxes, state spending and AI — and nearly two-thirds wanting the next governor to take the state in a new direction.
Just 36% gave Newsom’s overall performance an excellent or good rating in the survey conducted by TrueDot in collaboration with UC Berkeley’s Citrin Center and Politico.

Thanks for signing up!
The biggest group — 39% — rated his performance poor. Only 11% called it excellent.
The verdict was especially harsh on homelessness, where 72% said Newsom had handled the issue not too well or not at all well. Just a quarter offered a positive assessment.
Even voters in his own party gave him poor marks: Among Democrats and Democratic-leaning voters, 57% rated his handling of homelessness negatively.
Some 69% of voters rated Newsom’s handling of housing negatively, compared with 28% who said he had handled it well. That included 52% of Democrats and Democratic leaners giving him low marks.

Newsom spokesperson Izzy Gardon responded with a decidedly sunnier assessment, citing his electoral victories that included defeating a recall in 2021 and passing Proposition 50, last year’s congressional gerrymandering vote.

“Gavin Newsom overwhelmingly won five elections in eight years and is the most popular outgoing governor in the history of PPIC polling the question,” Gardon wrote in a text message to the California Post. “It’s a shame America’s Favorite Governor can’t run for another term — he’d crush it!”

Asked whether California’s next governor should generally continue Newsom’s policies or take the state in a different direction, 62% chose a change of course. Just 28% wanted Newsom’s policies to continue, while 10% were unsure.
Even among Democrats and Democratic leaners, fewer than half (49%) wanted the next governor to generally continue his policies. Another 37% preferred a different direction.

“Gov. Newsom frequently spins us around by saying California has the fourth largest economy in the world and has many firsts,” said Corrin Rankin, chairwoman of the California Republican Party. “But the reality of Newsom’s record of firsts are being number one in the country for the worst poverty, unemployment, cost-of-living, fraud, housing availability, income inequality and standardized test scores.”
Rankin blamed Newsom for students’ low test scores and college graduates being unable to “afford homes, pay their bills or get good jobs.”
“When 62% of Californians are unsatisfied with him, it’s easy to see that his presidential aspirations will be taking a ride on California’s high-speed rail to nowhere,” Rankin said.
Independents and other voters were more emphatic: 76% wanted a change, compared with just 11% who favored continuing Newsom’s approach.

Voters also gave Newsom poor marks on taxes and spending: Sixty percent rated his handling of taxes negatively, while 35% gave him positive marks. On state spending, over half offered a negative assessment and 39% a positive one.

Newsom also received negative marks on artificial intelligence regulation, with 43% saying he had handled the issue poorly, compared with 35% who said he had handled it well. Nearly a quarter were unsure.
Climate change supplied the lone bright spot. Half of voters said Newsom had handled the issue well, compared with 40% who disagreed.
Voters’ frustration with Newsom hasn’t translated into support for a Republican successor.
Democrat Xavier Becerra led Republican Steve Hilton 55% to 35% among likely voters, with 10% undecided.
Becerra’s campaign, which was endorsed by the current governor, did not respond to requests for comment on how his administration would differ from Newsom’s.
HiIton told The Post that poll findings show the last 16 years under Democratic governors — Newsom and former Gov. Jerry Brown — have been a “massive failure” and voters want change.

“The only way to get change is to vote for me as governor. Becerra would be four more years of one-party rule — but even worse than Newsom,” Hilton said. “He wouldn’t push back on any of the costs and craziness coming out of Sacramento. For everyone who is desperate for change and may be reluctant to vote Republican, I would say: Just try it.”
The online voter survey interviewed 1,149 California registered voters in English and Spanish from Oct. 9–14, including 909 likely voters.
The survey also exposed a gap between ordinary voters and the participating “policy influencers,” who were surveyed separately.

A separate survey of 213 influencers — who include political staffers, lobbyists, policy advisers and others dialed in to California politics, according to Politico — found they were more likely to back Newsom’s performance as governor.

Among those insiders, 52% rated Newsom’s overall performance excellent or good — compared with 36% of voters. They were also substantially more positive about his handling of taxes and climate change.
But even that crowd had its limits: 52% wanted California’s next governor to take a different direction.
